## Product scope

`codely` is the Tuanjie Codely / Tuanjie Cowork family from Unity China — an AI
agent for Unity and Tuanjie Engine game development.

- **Codely** = the agent itself (brain), built on `Codely CLI` + `Harness`.
  It owns Skills, Subagents, Extensions, LSP, and the `Codely Context` RAG KB.
- **Tuanjie Cowork** = the desktop client shell that replaces 团结 Hub, bundling
  Hub project management + Codely AI. It is one *access form* of Codely, not a
  separate product.
- Other access forms share the same `Codely CLI` + `Harness`: VSCode / Visual
  Studio / JetBrains extensions, the engine-embedded `CodelyBridge`, the pure
  `codely` CLI, and (in development) web and mobile clients.

All ends are based on the **same `Codely CLI` + `Harness`**, so context and
configuration are shared across ends. One `codely` entry therefore covers CLI,
Cowork desktop, engine-embedded, and IDE-extension surfaces.

## MCP configuration

MCP config lives inside the `settings.json` `mcpServers` key (there is no
separate `mcp.json`). Three transports are supported:

- **Stdio** (local process, low latency): `command` / `args` / `env` / `cwd`
- **SSE** (remote, auto-reconnect): `httpUrl` + `headers`
- **Streamable HTTP** (bidirectional, standard HTTP): `httpUrl` + `headers`

```jsonc
// Stdio
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "myLocal": {
      "command": "node",
      "args": ["/abs/path/server.js", "--port", "50206"],
      "env": { "API_KEY": "${API_TOKEN}" },
      "cwd": "/abs/path",
      "trust": true
    }
  }
}

// SSE / Streamable HTTP
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "remoteApi": {
      "httpUrl": "https://api.example.com/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ${API_TOKEN}" },
      "timeout": 5000
    }
  }
}
```

Real example from `~/.codely-cli/settings.json` on this machine:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "TJGenerators": { "httpUrl": "https://ai-generator.tuanjie.cn/mcp" }
  }
}
```

Config file locations (project overrides user):

- User: `~/.codely-cli/settings.json`
- Project: `<project>/.codely-cli/settings.json`

Commands and GUI:

- CLI: `codely mcp add <name> <url>`; verify with `/mcp list`, `/mcp reload`.
- GUI (Cowork / engine-embedded): type `/` → **Manage MCP Servers** → name +
  URL + Type (Stdio / SSE / Streamable HTTP); new session to apply. Reference
  MCP resources in chat with `@`.

## Skill configuration

A Skill is a directory; `SKILL.md` is required, the rest optional:

```
my-skill/
├── SKILL.md       # required: YAML frontmatter + Markdown body
├── scripts/       # optional: helper scripts
├── references/    # optional: reference docs (loaded on demand)
└── assets/        # optional: templates, resources
```

`SKILL.md` format — YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) + Markdown body:

```markdown
---
name: my-skill-name
description: When to use this skill and how (the trigger field).
---
## When to Use
- scenario bullets
## Instructions
- concrete steps and rules
## Examples
- usage examples
```

Storage paths and load priority (highest → lowest):

1. Project: `.codely-cli/skills/` (team-shared). At the same level,
   `.agents/skills/` takes priority over `.codely-cli/skills/`.
2. User: `~/.codely-cli/skills/` (personal, global).
3. Extension: skills bundled with an installed Extension.

Discovery and activation: on a new session the agent scans all paths, loads
only Skill names + descriptions, matches them to the request, asks for
confirmation, then loads the full content and executes. **You must start a new
session after creating or editing a Skill** for it to take effect.

Management commands: `/skills list | enable | disable | reload`, with
`--scope workspace` to scope to the project. Create one in chat with
`create a new skill called 'api-auditor'`.

> `CODELY.md` ≠ `SKILL.md`. `CODELY.md` is the project context/memory file
> (like `CLAUDE.md`), auto-loaded and generated by `/init unity`. It is the
> documented `rules` path above, not a Skill.

## Other context and memory forms

Beyond Skills and MCP, Codely keeps several context surfaces. These are product
state, not migration objects — treat them as manual reconstruction only (see
`migration-safety.md`):

- **Memory module** — persists context across sessions; the cross-session memory
  layer for the agent loop.
- **Codely Context** — a RAG-based, project-specific knowledge base so the agent
  learns your code conventions.
- **Unity Insight** — a SQLite-backed virtual filesystem (VFS) that indexes the
  Unity/Tuanjie project into a graph of entities (GameObjects, Components).
  Read-only analysis tools: `vfs_ls`, `vfs_glob`, `vfs_read`, `vfs_grep`,
  `vfs_refs` ("who references whom"). Insight sees; Unity Tools does.
- **CODELY.md Structured Memories** — the `CODELY.md` file carries
  `## Codely Structured Memories` sections (`User` / `Feedback` / `Project`)
  that persist durable facts across sessions.
- **Subagents** — a professional sub-agent system that parallelizes work (e.g.,
  one subagent for asset generation, one for tests).
- **Extensions** — the upgrade path over a Skill: one Extension can bundle
  multiple Skills, custom commands, MCP servers, themes, and hooks into a
  shareable, versioned package.
- **LSP** — language service that understands C# and engine APIs.

## Format conversion with `agent-skills-setup`

This is how the migration engine (`smart-ide-migration.sh`) actually handles
Codely, verified by code trace **and** an isolated temp-HOME end-to-end test
(2026-08-10, both directions, embedded `settings.json` + pre-existing target).

### Auto-convertible objects

| Object | Direction | Mechanism (verified) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **MCP** | codely ⇄ any `mcpServers` IDE | See "Embedded-config MCP" below |
| **Skills (global)** | codely ⇄ any | per-skill-dir `cp -r` from `~/.codely-cli/skills` + preflight + secret redaction |
| **Skills (project)** | codely ⇄ any | per-skill-dir `cp -r` from `.codely-cli/skills` (not in `project_skills_manual_only`) |
| **Rules (`CODELY.md`)** | codely → any | literal `cp` of `CODELY.md` → target rules file (see caveat) |

### Embedded-config MCP (the key mechanism)

Codely's MCP lives *inside* `settings.json` under `mcpServers` — it is **not** a
standalone `mcp.json`. The converter handles this without copying the whole
config file, because:

- **Source (codely → target):** the dispatch calls `read_path(data, "mcpServers")`
  and extracts **only** the `mcpServers` sub-tree from `settings.json`. The rest
  of `settings.json` (theme, model, other keys) is left untouched. This respects
  the `object-migration.md` rule "never copy whole config / opaque trees" — only
  the MCP sub-key is taken.
- **Target (other → codely):** the converter loads the existing
  `settings.json`, reads its current `mcpServers`, **merges** the incoming
  servers in, and writes back **only** the `mcpServers` sub-key. All other
  `settings.json` keys are preserved (non-destructive merge).
- **Transports:** codely has **no** `target_ide == "codely"` schema block, so
  stdio (`command`/`args`/`env`/`cwd`), SSE (`httpUrl`+`headers`), and Streamable
  HTTP (`httpUrl`+`headers`) shapes pass through **verbatim**.
- **Secrets:** `redact_node` clears literal credentials in `env`/`headers` and
  preserves symbolic `${ENV_VAR}` references — same as every `mcpServers` IDE.

> This is why codely MCP is **auto-convertible** while codely **config** is
> **manual-only** (below): the converter bites off exactly the `mcpServers`
> sub-key and never touches the rest of `settings.json`.

### Manual-only objects (by design, for all IDEs)

- **Config (`settings.json`):** `migrate_config` is manual-only for every IDE.
  Codely's `settings.json` is an opaque IDE config — do **not** copy it whole.
  Use the auto MCP extraction above as the safe subset.
- **Memory / Agents / Hooks:** manual-only. This covers Codely's Memory module,
  Codely Context (RAG), Unity Insight (VFS), `CODELY.md` Structured Memories
  (User/Feedback/Project), Subagents, Extensions, and LSP. These are
  product/runtime state; reconstruct them in the target workspace, do not copy.

### Conversion caveats

- **`.agents/skills/` priority is NOT auto-handled.** Codely loads
  `.agents/skills/` ahead of `.codely-cli/skills/` at the same level. The
  migrator only writes `.codely-cli/skills/` (from `ide-paths.json`). After a
  (target = codely) skill migration, verify which directory wins, and review
  same-name priority / trust manually.
- **`CODELY.md` Structured Memories are memory-like.** A literal `cp` of
  `CODELY.md` reproduces the `## Codely Structured Memories` block in the target
  rules file. Per `object-migration.md`, private/generated memory should not be
  blindly copied — review and rewrite only durable facts as rules manually.

### Empirical test results (temp-HOME, 2026-08-10)

- **codely → cursor (global):** `TJGenerators` SSE server (with
  `httpUrl`+`headers` and `Authorization: Bearer ${TJ_API_TOKEN}`) was extracted
  from `settings.json` and merged into the cursor target `mcp.json` alongside a
  pre-existing cursor server. `settings.json` source was **unchanged**.
- **cursor → codely (global):** a cursor stdio server was merged into the
  codely target `settings.json` `mcpServers`; the existing `theme`/`model` keys
  were **preserved**; a literal `env.API_KEY` was **redacted** to `""`.

## Migration notes

- `SKILL.md` uses the same open `name`/`description` + body convention adopted
  by Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI, and 40+ agents, so Skill content
  migrates cleanly across those targets.
- MCP uses the standard `mcpServers` key **embedded in `settings.json`** (not a
  separate `mcp.json`). The converter extracts/merges only that sub-key, so a
  Codely MCP entry maps to other `mcpServers` targets without translation and
  without copying the whole config (see "Format conversion" above).
- Do **not** migrate the memory module, Codely Context index, Unity Insight
  index, or generated `CODELY.md` Structured Memories — these are runtime/generated
  state. Reconstruct them manually in the target workspace.

Sources: [Tuanjie Codely overview](https://www.163.com/dy/article/L3JMDA2I0526E124.html), [Unity China developer post](https://developer.unity.cn/projects/6a7189bcedbc2a120fe6d4af), [Tuanjie Cowork](https://codely.tuanjie.cn/download), [AI environment setup](https://codely-docs.tuanjie.cn/learn/ai-programming-environment-setup-guide).
